key_insight: The paper argues that 3D-consistent world generation requires a geometry-native latent space, not just better image synthesis. By sharing a compact latent representation between perception and generation, the model can better preserve cross-view structure and scene consistency.
problem_solved: Current visual generators can create realistic images but often fail to maintain a coherent 3D scene across viewpoints. This paper addresses the mismatch between appearance-centric generative latents and geometry-aware perception latents.
method: Learn a compact latent space designed around geometry rather than appearance.
Use this shared representation as a common foundation for both perception and generation.
Reparameterize generation so it can produce 3D-consistent outputs while preserving photorealism.
impact: This work offers a path toward world models that are both visually realistic and structurally consistent across views. For practitioners, it could improve robotics, AR/VR, simulation, and any application needing reliable 3D scene understanding and generation.

paper_title: GAE: Learning a Geometry-Native Latent Space for 3D-Consistent World Generation
paper_authors: Jiahao Lu, Minghao Yin, Wenbo Hu, Hengyu Liu, Wang Zhao
